The issue occurs in the `SingularValueDecompositionImpl` class when calculating the singular values. The failing test case `testMath320A` creates a `RealMatrix` and expects the singular values to match a reference array with a specific precision. The bug report describes that the last singular value is expected to be very close to 0, but instead, it is reported as `NaN`.

Looking at the `SingularValueDecompositionImpl` class, the `getSingularValues` method simply returns a clone of the `singularValues` array without performing any calculations. This suggests that the calculation of the singular values might be incorrect or not properly initialized.

Further investigation is needed to determine why the last singular value is being reported as `NaN`. We also observed that the `getRowDimension()` method of the `RealMatrixImpl` class returns the number of rows in the matrix, which is relevant for understanding the matrix dimensions used in the singular value calculation.

Next, we need to analyze the singular value calculation logic in `SingularValueDecompositionImpl` to identify the root cause of the `NaN` singular value.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
